title: Al-Mulk, whole
tomorrow: who's wrapped in a blanket, and told to stand up at night?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the end of al-Hashr: a humbled mountain and the most beautiful names. Today closes the week with a surah for the end of the day.
screen: `THE MOST BEAUTIFUL NAMES.` → `A SURAH FOR THE END OF THE DAY.`

segments.voice: Lights off, phone face-down, the ceiling up there in the dark. A report in Tirmidhi says the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, wouldn't sleep until he'd recited al-Mulk, and some Muslims still read it at bedtime. It's a strange surah to fall asleep to, because it tells you to look up. In Pickthall's words: "Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts?"
screen: `LIGHTS OFF, PHONE DOWN.` → `READ BEFORE SLEEP.` → `THEN LOOK AGAIN.`

segments.voice: It opens: "Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things." Then why we're here: "Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct." Here's the detail to tell a friend: best, not most. The test is the quality of what you do, not the pile of it. Then the sky, and the dare: look again, then again and yet again, and your sight comes back to you tired, having found no crack. In the middle comes a plain question: "Should He not know what He created? And He is the Subtile, the Aware." Later: "Have they not seen the birds above them spreading out their wings and closing them? Naught upholdeth them save the Beneficent." Look again is the surah's whole method, and it fits the week. Al-Hujurat looked again at strangers: know one another. Ya-Sin looked again at old bones: be, and it is. Ar-Rahman looked again at every gift: which favors? Al-Waqi'ah looked again at a glass of water: the foremost. Al-Hadid looked again at a new address: with you. Al-Hashr looked again at a single name and found many: the most beautiful names. Every passage asked for a second look at something ordinary. Al-Mulk asks for it at bedtime, when the day is done and there's finally time.
screen: `BEST, NOT MOST.` · `LOOK AGAIN, AND YET AGAIN.` · `BIRDS, HELD UP.` · `A WEEK OF SECOND LOOKS.` · then, large: `LOOK AGAIN.`

segments.voice: Look up: a ceiling, a window, a sky if you can see one. Look once and take it in. Then look again, slower, the way the surah asks, and find one thing you missed the first time. For the rest of the sit, keep looking gently.
Al-Mulk. The Dominion: surah 67, the surah of best conduct, held-up birds, and a sky you're dared to look at twice.
Last line of the week: look again, six passages and six second looks under one sky. Sleep well.

howItsDone: Some Muslims recite Surah al-Mulk every night before sleeping, following reports in Tirmidhi about the Prophet's practice; it is short enough to read from memory in bed.
